title: Design a Distributed Crossword Search Service
prompt: Design a service that solves crossword grids against a dictionary using distributed search. Cover grid parsing, slot/crossing constraints, propagation, dynamic work splitting, leases/retries, global completion, cancellation, and proof that an unsatisfiable grid has no remaining work.

response.placeholder: Start with constraint propagation locally; distribute only durable subtrees that are still broad enough to justify it.
response.reference_answer:
## Solver core
Parse slots and crossings, index words by length/pattern, choose the most constrained slot, propagate letter constraints, and backtrack. A state contains grid assignments, remaining domains, dictionary generation, and a deterministic subtree ID.

## Distributed work
The coordinator splits only broad branches after propagation, persists subtrees, and leases them to workers. Workers checkpoint progress; lease expiry permits duplicate exploration, which is safe because subtree IDs and result claims are idempotent. Use a global winner CAS and cancellation epoch once a solution is found.

## Completion
Unsatisfiable is valid only after every durable subtree is terminal and no lease remains. Coordinator loss is recovered from the task ledger; workers can be replaced without losing the search frontier.

## Progressive Hints
1. Split on a constrained branch, not arbitrary depth.
2. Duplicate work is safer than lost work.
3. A local empty queue does not prove global unsatisfiability.
